newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ARMY OF BARCELONA COACHES COST $8 MLN A YEAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARMY OF BARCELONA COACHES COST $8 MLN A YEAR.

text.p: Barcelona pay a group of thirty coaches and scouts around a billion pesetas ($7.8 million) a year, the Spanish sports daily As reported on Thursday.

First team manager Bobby Robson's expensive support staff includes two assistants, a trainer, physiotherapist and goalkeeper coach while the club employs no fewer than eight scouts, amongst them one in Brazil, it said.
A dozen more coaches look after 10 youth teams and Barcelona B and C, which play in Spain's second and third divisions respectively.
Among a group of outside advisers are former Barcelona and Argentine national coach Cesar Menotti and Spanish manager Javier Clemente, widely seen as a future Barcelona coach.
A club spokesman refused to comment on the figures, but denied that Menotti and Clemente were on the club payroll.
